paragraphs: Stevenage is in Hertfordshire, so children in care from the town are looked after by Hertfordshire County Council's not-for-profit fostering service and by the agencies shown above. The council's fostering team has offices in Stevenage, where most of its training courses are held, and it is part of Foster East, a group of councils in the East of England that share out-of-hours support.

Hertfordshire says it is short of carers for brothers and sisters: more than half of its children in care are siblings, and 56% of sibling groups are split up. It also needs emergency carers who take a child for around ten days, long-term carers, usually for children aged seven and over, carers for separated migrant children, who are usually teenagers, and carers for its NEST scheme for children who would otherwise live in a children's home.

You need to be over 21 and in good general health, with at least one spare bedroom; you can keep working and you do not need to be a parent. The council describes a social worker with monthly supervision, a carer buddy, support at any hour, preparation and core training, and an annual review.

The council advertises a weekly allowance of up to £468 for each child, plus a weekly skills payment, mileage, a setting-up fee, holiday and birthday allowances and a uniform allowance. Emergency carers receive a daily retainer, and NEST carers a higher skills payment. Its next online information evening is on 10 December 2026.
Our Hertfordshire page covers the whole county, and our Hitchin and Luton pages cover the places nearby. Talk to the council's team and to two or three of the services above before you decide.
